matches.reason: Same problem: worktrees have no node_modules/, so the ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/node_modules rumdl path and the worktree-session criterion can't both pass.
Same recommendation to split the lint swap, LSP plugin, and docs into separate tasks. Its rationale is WIP/ownership rather than growth from 7 to 13 criteria, but the problem is the same.
Same evidence-rule problem: the worktree-session criterion has no re-runnable command and 'record in Handoff' can't fail. It omits the docs-criterion-as-judgment point, but the core matches.

About criterion 4's planted-error check, but the problem raised is the lack of a lasting regression guard, not that the verifier needs a self-contained command to rerun it (key 6). Only partial overlap. It also doesn't address LSP diagnostics matching the gate (key 4).

Version-pinning of rumdl 0.2.77. It mentions the untested ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} expansion only as a side point. It doesn't say that a criterion locks in the unverified marketplace-plugin mechanism (key 3).
CI coverage of the binary. No key item covers this.
Discoverability of the new doc from CLAUDE.md. No key item covers this.
Doc staleness and recording the rumdl version. No key item covers this.
A checked-and-fine note (plugin trust), so it is not a finding. Its aside on the marketplace trust prompt touches key 3 only tangentially.

Decision item 3 asks the user to approve the .claude/settings.json change as part of approving the task, which is the same point as key 7. Items 1 (is the LSP needed now) and 2 (split, which duplicates finding 2/key 1) don't match anything else.

citations.evidence: Every worktree still installs its own dependencies, builds its own artifacts, and starts its own services.
Atomic PR discipline keeps one logical change per PR, under 400 lines.
Kiro turned a small bug fix into sixteen acceptance criteria
The evidence bundle shown to the developer is a SELECT, not a self-reported summary... if the INSERT did not happen, the check did not happen.
Wrap agent output in hard, deterministic checks — linting, schema validation, CI gates — that enforce correctness regardless of what the agent produces.
The agent misunderstands a requirement early and builds on the faulty premise, reinforcing the wrong assumption until the error is too expensive to unwind.
CI checks run after a commit is pushed, providing a second layer independent of the local environment.
Keep AGENTS.md to ~100 lines as a pointer map into a versioned docs/ directory
AI configuration files drift out of sync with the code they describe; the agent loads stale guidance as authoritative context
Vetting a plugin at install says nothing about version 1.1. The harness re-reads that plugin's lifecycle-hook config on every update
Add instructions when you've identified a recurring problem they would solve.
